claims.claim_text_verbatim: We show that a simple alternative, Semi-OPD, which distills from offline rollouts generated by the initial student, can often outperform OPD in both accuracy and training efficiency.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD distills offline initial-student rollouts and often outperforms OPD in accuracy and efficiency.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across 17 teacher–student pairs ranging from 1.5B to 235B parameters, Semi-OPD outperforms OPD in 14 cases, with up to +13.6% accuracy and 11.4× training speedup.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD beats OPD on 14 of 17 teacher-student pairs, gaining up to +13.6% accuracy and 11.4× speedup.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We further find that the choice between OPD and Semi-OPD depends on the alignment between the initial teacher and student, quantified by an output-token overlap ratio: OPD is beneficial only when the two are highly aligned with high overlap ratios.
claims.claim_summary: OPD is only beneficial over Semi-OPD when initial teacher-student output-token overlap is high.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our deeper investigation suggests that effective distillation requires on-policyness w.r.t. both the student and the teacher.
claims.claim_summary: Effective distillation requires on-policyness with respect to both student and teacher distributions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For misaligned pairs, student rollouts can become increasingly off-policy w.r.t. the teacher as context length grows, weakening the distillation signal.
claims.claim_summary: Misaligned student rollouts grow off-policy relative to the teacher over longer contexts, weakening supervision.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In contrast, Semi-OPD is often more stable, as it distills on shorter contexts while covering full trajectories and exposing the student to more teacher-preferred tokens.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD is more stable by distilling shorter contexts while covering full trajectories.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our Semi-OPD achieves much improved/comparable accuracy for teacher–student pairs with low/high overlap, respectively, while reducing training time by up to 11.4× over OPD.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD achieves improved or comparable accuracy while reducing training time by up to 11.4×.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We find that Semi-OPD outperforms OPD on 14 of them, with up to +13.6% accuracy and 11.4× training speedup as shown in Fig. 1, and achieves comparable performance (within a 0.1%–2.6% gap) on the remaining three.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD outperforms OPD on 14 pairs and remains within 0.1%–2.6% on the other 3.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: OPD is only useful for aligned teacher–student pairs with high overlap in output tokens; for misaligned pairs, Semi-OPD is a better alternative in both accuracy and training efficiency.
claims.claim_summary: OPD helps only high-overlap pairs, whereas Semi-OPD is superior for misaligned pairs.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Effective distillation requires both the on-policyness of training rollout w.r.t. the student and closeness to the teacher; OPD prioritizes the former but may sacrifice the latter.
claims.claim_summary: OPD prioritizes student on-policyness at the expense of closeness to the teacher.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The difference is especially pronounced for Qwen3 thinking-mode pairs: OPD undergoes a substantial performance collapse during training, whereas Semi-OPD continues to improve.
claims.claim_summary: On Qwen3 thinking pairs, OPD collapses during training while Semi-OPD steadily improves.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: on the Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking) and Qwen3-4B (non-thinking) students, which have low teacher–student overlap ratios, Semi-OPD outperforms all other baselines in accuracy while also being the most efficient, e.g., achieving +7.1% and +8.8% higher accuracy with 35× and 19.5× less training time than Relay-OPD on the two pairs, respectively, according to Fig. 1 and Tab. 4.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD outperforms all baselines on low-overlap Qwen3 non-thinking pairs with dramatic speedups over Relay-OPD.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On the Nemotron-Cascade-2 pair, which has a high overlap ratio of approximately 89%, our Semi-OPD remains competitive with other OPD baselines and falls only slightly behind the best baseline by 0.7% accuracy, while reducing the training time by 2.2x as compared to FastOPD and 4.5x compared to OPD.
claims.claim_summary: On high-overlap Nemotron-Cascade-2, Semi-OPD is competitive within 0.7% of best baseline while training 2.2x-4.5x faster.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our Semi-OPD without the additional teacher-rollout SFT stage can outperform Semi-OPD with this stage, indicating that SFT on teacher rollouts is unnecessary.
claims.claim_summary: Teacher-rollout SFT before Semi-OPD is unnecessary and actually hurts final performance.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Semi-OPD consistently outperforms teacher-rollout distillation.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD consistently beats distilling directly on teacher-generated rollouts.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: increasing the rollout cap can hurt the low-overlap pair while benefiting the higher-overlap pair.
claims.claim_summary: Increasing training rollout length limits harms low-overlap pairs but helps high-overlap pairs.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: restricting supervision to the first quarter substantially slows convergence and reduces final accuracy, whereas training on full trajectories achieves the best peak accuracy.
claims.claim_summary: Truncating supervision to rollout prefixes reduces accuracy compared to training on full trajectories.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Semi-OPD exposes the student to more teacher-preferred tokens, i.e., more on-policy w.r.t. the teacher, whereas OPD more often produces signals that suppress the student’s own sampled tokens.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD exposes students to more teacher-preferred tokens than standard OPD.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Importantly, Semi-OPD also outperforms OPD under top-k reverse KL, as shown in Fig. 8, indicating that its advantage is not specific to the sampled-token objective.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD's advantages over OPD hold under top-k reverse KL distillation objectives.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: on low-overlap pairs, regardless of initialization, all runs eventually converge to the performance level reached by OPD initialized from the initial student model under the same rollout cap, while the warm start only affects the convergence trajectory.
claims.claim_summary: OPD on low-overlap pairs converges to the same accuracy equilibrium regardless of warm-start initialization.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: for a high-overlap pair, as shown in Fig. 10, switching from Semi-OPD to OPD improves performance and closes most of the gap with OPD applied from scratch.
claims.claim_summary: Switching to OPD after Semi-OPD on high-overlap pairs recovers performance of OPD from scratch.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Fig. 11, models distilled only on math-heavy datasets [26] also improve on HumanEval and HumanEval+, with Semi-OPD remaining ahead of OPD.
claims.claim_summary: Math-distilled Semi-OPD models transfer improvements to coding tasks like HumanEval better than OPD.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: with a base student, the initial rollouts are too weak and Semi-OPD underperforms OPD; with an instruction-tuned student, Semi-OPD regains its advantage.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD requires an instruction-tuned student with sufficiently competent initial rollouts to beat OPD.
